newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK plans to speed up domestic gas competition.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK plans to speed up domestic gas competition.

text.p: Britain's Conservative government on Monday outlined plans to speed up the timetable for extension of competition in the domestic gas market to allow consumers nationwide to choose suppliers as early as April 1998.

But the plans, announced by Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang, drew criticism from the opposition Labour party which said it might delay the extension if it came to power at a general election in May.
Lang said competition, already introduced in parts of the south and west of England under a pilot scheme, would be extended to Scotland and Northeast England as early as October.

It would then be spread south in five instalments in the rest of England and Wales in 1998. If computer systems were ready in time new regions would be opened to competition in January in monthly instalments.

Lang said following Northeast England and Scotland competition would be available to North and Northwest England, Midlands and South Yorkshire, Wales and west Midlands and Wiltshire, Southeast and Eastern England and finally to all remaining regions.
"I want to keep up the momentum we now have by giving domestic gas customers the chance to benefit from savings of around 20 percent on British Gas' standard tariffs," said Lang.
Originally plans for extended competition were not expected to start until next year.
Gas watchdog the Office of Gas Supply (Ofgas) said it welcomed speeding up the process.
"We've long been in favour of introducing the benefits of competition, and rather sooner than later," said an Ofgas spokesman.
But opposition Labour, firm favourites in the polls to take power from the ruling Conservatives, said it questioned the new timetable.

"If elected Labour will look at today's proposal to change the timetable to see if it is the best way of introducing gas competition at the earliest practical time," said Labour energy spokesman John Battle.
Labour said it would continue to support the introduction of competition in the gas sector.
But Battle said it might decide to spend more time examining the results of the pilot scheme and consulting with the industry, the regulators and consumers.

A number of gas supply companies already have Ofgas-issued licences to supply gas to domestic consumers anywhere in the country, and will be able to do so as soon as deregulation is permitted in other regions.

These are British Gas Trading, part of Centrica Plc ; Eastern Natural Gas; London Total Energy; Northern Electric Plc; NORWEB; Southern Electric Gas ; Scottish Power Plc, for everywhere except the first pilot area; and Texaco Inc and Calor Group Plc, trading as Calortex.
